name: f4-visible-delivery-v1
hypothesis: Reviews and promotion respond mainly to visible Output and recognised results; making Prepare report materials, High-intensity work and Showcase/Report/Fight-for-resources the default, interrupted only when a qualitative wellbeing floor is breached, yields better review grades, earlier promotions and higher salary-driven Wealth and Level than balanced or invest-first play, outweighing the wellbeing cost.
predicted_behaviour: Highest share of Output-producing Energy and main actions of all families; most High-intensity work; best early review grades (more A/S, fewer C/D) and the earliest first promotion; recovery appears in bursts triggered by floor breaches rather than steadily; lower end-of-run Health/Dignity than F1 and F5; higher risk of health-direction elimination than F1.
refutation: Refuted if F4's review grades and final Level are not better than F1 and F2 on paired runs, or if its mean quantitative_score is below F1 with more eliminations. Manipulation fails if floor breaches occur so often that its Output-action share is not clearly higher than F1's.
notes: The wellbeing floor is defined qualitatively (lower part of the published 0–10 range, falling trend, warnings, Network near zero, Wealth below zero). Review cadence is the published six-month schedule.
